profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer I at Enova International

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer I
positions.description: - Design, develop, and test software for the Small and Medium Business Decisions team.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
- Designed, developed, and tested back-end code for HCL Sametime meeting software, based on a Node, MongoDB, and Docker tech stack.
- Implemented meeting style customization, enabling users to create lecture and confidential meetings.
- Pioneered development on functional test suite for Sametime back-end functionality using the Gatling performance testing framework in Scala, enabling more robust verification of program correctness

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
- Designed, developed, and tested new features, improvements, and defect resolutions for HCL Launch/IBM UrbanCode Deploy, a Dev Ops automation tool built with a Java and SQL back-end and a Dojo front-end. 
- Provide customer support to dozens of global clients by analyzing the customer's circumstances and devising a resolution to the issue, successfully closed more tickets than other rotating members of the team.
- Serve as a client advocate for a major customer, acting as a liaison to advise on specific configurations/solutions, to escalate severity on active support issues, and to educate the customer on upcoming updates to the product.

positions.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Teaching Assistant for EECS 325 Computer Networks I

- Held office hours, answered student questions via email, and assisted in grading assignments, projects, and exams for the class.

positions.title: Student Assistant
positions.description:
- Improved efficiency in the Information Security Office through document summary, coordination with faculty and student organizations, and data entry. 

- Increased CWRU community knowledge and adherence to information security practices through speeches to organizations, individual meetings with students, distribution of fliers, and outreach to students. This has helped guide students on properly reporting phishing emails. 

- Developed excellent professional interpersonal skills by communicating with faculty, students, and on-campus organization for National Cyber Security Month and through security talks to clubs 

I have worked this on-campus job Fall 2015 through Fall 2017, and I returned to this job (after my co-op) in Fall 2018.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
- Developed, designed and tested software for the Commercial Banking line of business as part of Project Catalyst, an effort to modernize CRM. 
- Improved developer time efficiency by creating internal tools to assist in Salesforce data imports and synchronization of source information on test instances.
- Learned the Salesforce Platform tech stack: Apex, Visualforce, and Lightning Web Components. 
- Greatly improved knowledge of SDLC and Scrum.

positions.title: Software Developer Co-Op
positions.description:
- Participate in Agile software development life cycle to develop features, generate improvements, and fix defects in the IBM/HCL Technologies UrbanCode Deploy product, contributing to two major product releases

As a Software Developer Co-op, I worked as a regular member of my team, primarily adding minor features and fixing bugs. However, my work items often involved various technologies adjacent to regular software development. For example, I worked on several items on making scripts work across different Linux distributions' default shells, exposing me to many terminals. Another example, I had to configure adding a authorization group in our product through an LDAP connection, and this item forced me to learn about directory protocols. 

I also gained significant web development experience, especially with REST endpoints and a general MVC architecture. I value this experience most.

Formerly IBM UrbanCode

positions.title: IT Point-of-Sale Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Two separate internships

- Collaborated on the IT infrastructure team to design, code, debug, test, and maintain technical code, configuration, and documentation for point of sale (POS) systems.  I participated in the change control process to mitigate risk system errors across all of IT. 

During my internship, I self-taught Python to assist the Senior POS Engineer with automating log clean up and delivering alert messages via SMTP to notify of errors in processing logs. The alert messages helped the Senior POS Engineer to begin to aggregate recurring error messages to begin root cause analysis. 

Additionally, using my basic knowledge of crytography, I assisted with migrating electronic payments authentication software from an old server, moving it much closer to being decommissioned. 

During my second internship, I returned to my role and performed many of the same functions with a more in-depth interaction with the IBM/Toshiba 4690 OS. I programmed TLogChecker, which monitors the previous day's record of transactions to check for changes in file size. This program alerts the POS team after detection to recommend a collection of system logs to troubleshoot the issue. This development process meant that I had to learn how to work around limitations of a nearly 20 year old operating system designed for POS. 

I also learned Powershell to help automate the almost daily change control process of At Home. The three scripts, referred to as ChangeSuite, periodically send emails informing configured members of IT infrastructure the current items to discuss. It also sends reminders to approvers if they have neglected to approve an item, and it also sends emails to technicians reminding them that their change has been approved. 

- Previously: June 2016 - July 2016; May 2017 - July 2017

volunteerExperiences.description: One-on-one tutoring with 3rd grade students at a low-income elementary school in Dallas, Texas. Tutoring focused on literacy.

During my years on the Jesuit Debate Team, we would volunteer by helping the Dallas Urban Debate Alliance to host tournaments that would encourage middle school students and students from lower-income high schools to participate in Policy Debate.

projects.title: Weiver
projects.description: A hackathon project built in Java with two other team members (no LinkedIn profiles) that aggregates phone reviews for frequent terms from multiple tech review websites. 95% complete except for some errors that we could not resolve by the end of the hackathon. In this project, I spent most of my time in a sort of project manager role, determining the class structure and debugging. And I also took an active role in debugging others' code.

projects.title: handrite.io
projects.description:
Submission for EECS 395 Senior Project. 
handrite.io is a web application which helps to teach children handwriting with machine learning. It allows parents/children to track progress across a variety of text samples.

organizations.name: Hacker Society (Association of Computing Machinery)
organizations.description:
Computer Science interest group that coordinates mentoring, professional development, events, and tech talks by students, alumni, and companies. 

As co-maintainer for the Fall 2019 semester, I must schedule and organize tech talks and activities by reaching out to the community and alumni.
